items.title: The number of geometric branches at a point is invariant under extension of the base field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the number of geometric branches of a locally algebraic k-scheme X at a point equals that of its base change X_K at any point lying above it. The proof compares the normalizations of X and Y = X_K in the commutative square of X^nu, Y^nu and X^nu_K, uses the cited normalization-and-change-of-fields lemma to see that one arrow is a universal homeomorphism and hence induces purely inseparable residue field extensions, and then rewrites both branch numbers as sums of separable degrees of residue field extensions over the normalizations (proof lines 8617-8633). The statement is finally reduced to the algebra fact that the sum of separable degrees over the quotient fields of m tensor_kappa l equals [m : kappa]_s, which the author derives by interpreting both sides as numbers of connected components using a separably closed base change (proof lines 8634-8655). H2: the reduction to the algebra fact and the connected-component interpretation are the non-routine steps, and the proof contains a commutative diagram.
